rules.sentence: Secondary osteosarcomas arise in abnormal bone, most commonly in individuals older than 50 around the knee or hip joint.[23]
The histology varies between subtypes, but the distinguishing features of osteoid production, variable nuclei with pleomorphism, and numerous mitoses are present.

The 2020 WHO classification subdivided secondary osteosarcoma into 6 subtypes: osteosarcoma in Paget's disease of bone, radiation-associated osteosarcoma, infarct-related osteosarcoma, osteosarcoma dye to chronic osteomyelitis, implant-related osteosarcoma and osteosarcoma associated with disorders like fibrous dysplasia.[20]
